nodes.label: CI
nodes.rationale: CI installs pinned dependencies and runs lint, types, unit tests, and production build with development login disabled.

nodes.label: Foundation auth and home
nodes.rationale: Operate-first shared-journal surface selected from concept C; semantic HTML/CSS implements controls without generated decorative chrome.

nodes.label: Relationship thread
nodes.rationale: A single content-led thread connects plans, ideas, and memories instead of equal dashboard cards.

nodes.label: Bucket lists continuity
nodes.rationale: Extends the verified Shared-Journal Thread: list controls beside ideas on desktop, stacked on mobile, with real server actions.

nodes.label: One more dream lived
nodes.rationale: Completion bridges into a memory without requiring memory creation before an idea is complete.

nodes.label: Plans and memories continuity
nodes.rationale: A completed plan becomes a memory with provenance; calendar, media, checklist, and reminder surfaces remain unresolved.

nodes.label: Agent Instructions
nodes.rationale: Repository-wide product truth, skill routing, implementation, and verification policy.

nodes.label: Product Source of Truth
nodes.rationale: Read product, architecture, and relevant specifications; reconcile stale code or documented decisions in the same change.

nodes.label: Phase Completion Gate
nodes.rationale: Implementation is incomplete until applicable tests, migration evidence, advisors, visual checks, secret scanning, and documentation pass.

nodes.label: Skill Routing
nodes.rationale: Impeccable handles UI; Supabase and Postgres skills handle data; Graphify queries and updates cross-file knowledge.

nodes.label: Design System
nodes.rationale: Shipped visual truth for Us Together, distinct from pre-build design intent.

nodes.label: Shared-Journal Thread
nodes.rationale: A modern private letter meets a shared calendar; relationship continuity structures the UI.

nodes.label: One Wine Voice Rule
nodes.rationale: Deep wine is the single primary action and active emphasis color.

nodes.label: Warm Dark Rule
nodes.rationale: Dark mode retains warm plum, rose, and paper relationships rather than blue-black neutrals.

nodes.label: Serif Tells the Story Rule
nodes.rationale: Editorial serif carries relationship hierarchy while sans-serif carries controls and explanations.

nodes.label: One Narrative Path Rule
nodes.rationale: A dominant next relationship step prevents equal-card administrative layouts.

nodes.label: Bounded Paper Rule
nodes.rationale: Prefer tonal shifts and fine borders; reserve shadow for large paper, primary action, and thread markers.

nodes.label: Radius Follows Scale Rule
nodes.rationale: Controls, panels, and whole-page surfaces use progressively larger established radii.

nodes.label: Us Together
nodes.rationale: Private shared web space for exactly two active partners, with individual accounts and explicit couple membership.

nodes.label: Dream-to-Memory
nodes.rationale: Dream to Plan to Experience to Memory to Our Story connects features rather than isolated CRUD modules.

nodes.label: Dream-to-Memory MVP
nodes.rationale: Auth, pairing, dashboard, bucket lists, plans/calendar/reminders, memories/media, wishlists, notes, milestones, notifications, lifecycle and PWA.

nodes.label: Release 2
nodes.rationale: Vault, advanced notes, Know Me, Our Story, Google Calendar, push, search and richer realtime are deferred beyond MVP.

nodes.label: Later roadmap
nodes.rationale: Suggestions, questions, trip planning, AI assistance, and native apps require later decisions.

nodes.label: Privacy is behavior
nodes.rationale: Unauthorized content must be unqueryable, not merely hidden in the interface.

nodes.label: Accessibility and Inclusion
nodes.rationale: Targets WCAG 2.2 AA, keyboard/screen readers, reduced motion, non-color state cues, and inclusive relationship assumptions.

nodes.label: Us Together project overview
nodes.rationale: Phase 1-4 implementation and Plans/Memories slices exist on managed Supabase; application deployment is pending.

nodes.label: Current stack
nodes.rationale: Next.js App Router, strict TypeScript, React, Tailwind, customized shadcn, Supabase, Zod, Lucide and Vercel.

nodes.label: Paired developer fixture
nodes.rationale: Clearly fictional Alex and Maya session provides deterministic browser checks and is forcibly disabled in production.

nodes.label: API and Server Contracts
nodes.rationale: Server identity, Zod boundaries, domain-safe DTOs and non-disclosing error responses define public interfaces.

nodes.label: Server Actions
nodes.rationale: Default first-party mutation interface; route handlers serve callbacks, webhooks, exports and upload/signing needs.

nodes.label: Domain-safe DTO
nodes.rationale: Never return raw hidden columns or accept trusted client ownership fields; private existence may map to NOT_FOUND.

nodes.label: Pairing contracts
nodes.rationale: Private authenticated functions behind public invoker wrappers implement hashed codes, rate limits, cooldown, revocation and leave.

nodes.label: mutateBucket
nodes.rationale: Zod-discriminated create/rename/delete list; create/update/delete/complete idea; and versioned step operations derive server ownership.

nodes.label: filterBucketItems
nodes.rationale: Validated list/status/priority/category filters stay in request bodies; bounded pages use twelve rows and UUID cursor.

nodes.label: Bucket conversion
nodes.rationale: Source-locked security-invoker RPCs return existing linked plans or completed-idea memories on retry.

nodes.label: Plan contracts
nodes.rationale: Server validates local date/time and IANA zone, rejects DST gaps/invalid intervals and uses integer minor units.

nodes.label: Memory contracts
nodes.rationale: Direct and completed-source memory creation preserve provenance; upload finalization and signed URL actions remain unavailable.

nodes.label: Notification contracts
nodes.rationale: Generic envelopes hold safe target pointers; reading a target repeats authorization rather than trusting inbox content.

nodes.label: Idempotency and concurrency
nodes.rationale: Unique logical keys, row locks and versions enforce retries and concurrent invariants; check-then-insert is insufficient.

nodes.label: Database Specification
nodes.rationale: Normalized PostgreSQL entities, ownership, constraints, RLS, access indexes, deletion and migration workflow.

nodes.label: Identity and tenancy
nodes.rationale: Profiles, couples, active memberships and hashed invitations separate identity from shared ownership; capacity is transactional.

nodes.label: Bucket lists
nodes.rationale: Couple-owned lists contain versioned ideas and ordered steps; maximum 100 lists and 50 steps per idea.

nodes.label: Versioned bucket edits
nodes.rationale: Parent locking, monotonic version and complete permutation validation reject stale writes; deferrable positions permit atomic reorder.

nodes.label: Preserved provenance
nodes.rationale: Deleting an idea cascades steps but nulls source links on preserved plans and memories; populated lists cannot be deleted.

nodes.label: Plans
nodes.rationale: Normalized plans/checklists/reminders retain bucket source, UTC intervals, source timezone, location and money.

nodes.label: Memories
nodes.rationale: Memories/tags/tag links/media preserve source relationships and private object metadata without opaque JSON application state.

nodes.label: Wishlist purchase secrets
nodes.rationale: Purchaser-owned rows are separate from owner-readable wishlist data; only a different active partner may create them.

nodes.label: Notes visibility
nodes.rationale: Shared notes are member-readable, private notes author-only, and surprise recipients require a trusted reveal condition.

nodes.label: Notifications
nodes.rationale: Recipient-owned generic events also require active membership; mutable client state is limited to read status.

nodes.label: RLS access matrix
nodes.rationale: Ownership-aware SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE policies prevent inference, reassignment and former-member access.

nodes.label: Private memory storage
nodes.rationale: Object path includes couple and memory identifiers but authorization proves matching metadata and current active membership.

nodes.label: Index strategy
nodes.rationale: Indexes follow access patterns and query plans, including tenant/status/category/cursor and RLS predicates.

nodes.label: Deletion and retention
nodes.rationale: Leaving immediately ends RLS access while continuing members retain shared history; populated deletion/export remains controlled later work.

nodes.label: Architectural Decisions
nodes.rationale: Accepted decisions cover multi-tenancy, release boundaries, managed hosting, auth, privacy, design, workflows and continuity.

nodes.label: Multi-tenant couple ownership
nodes.rationale: ADR-001 keeps individuals, couples and memberships distinct; shared rows carry couple_id with immutable private ownership where needed.

nodes.label: Managed Vercel and Supabase
nodes.rationale: ADR-003 targets managed hosting without self-hosting portability as an MVP requirement; ADR-014 updates local workflow expectations.

nodes.label: Database-first authorization
nodes.rationale: ADR-005 relies on RLS and Storage policies supplemented by server workflows, never client filtering.

nodes.label: Protected vault not E2EE
nodes.rationale: ADR-007 uses private storage and temporary unlock authorization; infrastructure can process plaintext and must not claim zero knowledge.

nodes.label: Provenance-first plans and memories slice
nodes.rationale: ADR-011 exposes a secure continuity slice early without declaring skipped phase gates complete or shipping fake controls.

nodes.label: Couple leave and empty-space deletion
nodes.rationale: ADR-012 ends departing membership immediately, retains shared history for continuing member, restricts deletion to empty one-member spaces.

nodes.label: Content-minimal dashboard notifications
nodes.rationale: ADR-013 prevents private titles, bodies and secret counts leaking into previews; target authorization is checked again on open.

nodes.label: Hosted verification and deferred pairing
nodes.rationale: ADR-014 accepts hosted migrations, rollback-only fictional RLS tests and advisors without Docker/Podman. Save project reference only in ignored config, verify identity before writes, and defer real pairing to final integration.

nodes.label: Versioned bucket edits and transactional continuity
nodes.rationale: ADR-015 combines normalized steps, parent versions, source-locking conversions, database-derived completion and preserved downstream history. Sequential evidence is not simultaneous-session proof.

nodes.label: Open product and architecture decisions
nodes.rationale: Billing, legal retention, final identity, measured quotas, rich text, background jobs and AI consent/provider policy remain undecided.

nodes.label: Implementation Plan
nodes.rationale: Phased deployable delivery with explicit dependencies, exit gates and honest evidence.

nodes.label: Phase 0 Documentation baseline
nodes.rationale: Complete: specifications, release classification, terminology and contradiction mapping.

nodes.label: Phase 1 Foundation
nodes.rationale: Implementation and hosted migrations exist; historical local-runtime blockers are superseded by ADR-014, with clean replay still open.

nodes.label: Phase 2 Couple system and onboarding
nodes.rationale: Lifecycle implementation complete; real two-account and concurrent-final-slot verification deferred, not passed.

nodes.label: Phase 3 Dashboard and milestones
nodes.rationale: Implemented shared projections, milestones and generic notifications; earlier RLS suites not all rerun in Phase 4.

nodes.label: Phase 4 Bucket lists
nodes.rationale: Implemented CRUD, steps, filters, completion and retry-safe conversion; hosted 33 assertions pass while full integration/replay gates remain open.

nodes.label: Phase 5 Plans and internal calendar
nodes.rationale: Provenance-first slice exists; full CRUD, month/week calendar, checklist/reminder editing and delivery remain open.

nodes.label: Phase 6 Memories and media
nodes.rationale: Story-first slice and storage boundaries exist; uploads, inspection, derivatives, signed viewers, cleanup and full CRUD remain open.

nodes.label: Phase 7 Wishlists and notes
nodes.rationale: Planned owner/partner visibility, purchaser secrets, shared/private notes and inference auditing.

nodes.label: Phase 8 MVP completion
nodes.rationale: Planned full lifecycle/export/settings, release hardening, clean replay and final acceptance.

nodes.label: Phase 4 verification
nodes.rationale: Hosted migrations, generated types, 33 negative assertions, zero retained fixtures and indexed query evidence with explicit limits.

nodes.label: Rollback-only pgTAP verification
nodes.rationale: Read-only connector query endpoint necessitates a verification migration whose nested subtransaction rolls back both failures and success fixtures.

nodes.label: Migration identity correspondence
nodes.rationale: Connector timestamps differ from local filenames; map by names/source SQL and avoid duplicate pushes to already-migrated hosted project.

nodes.label: Phase 4 negative suite
nodes.rationale: 33 passed assertions cover cross-couple/former-member isolation, immutable ownership, stale reorder, progress, retries, completion actor and preserved downstream records.

nodes.label: Indexed bucket query
nodes.rationale: EXPLAIN chooses bucket_items_category_idx for couple/category/cursor; status remains a filter, not a production latency benchmark.

nodes.label: Phase 4 advisor findings
nodes.rationale: No new Phase 4 security finding; invitation no-policy is intentional RPC-only, leaked-password protection remains disabled, unused indexes informational.

nodes.label: Phase 4 browser evidence
nodes.rationale: Fictional development sessions exercise real server actions on desktop/mobile with keyboard/reduced motion; five browser tests pass with one intentional desktop skip for a mobile-only check. Lint, types, 28 unit tests and production build pass; detector is clear and fresh visual review fixes are applied. This is not hosted-auth evidence.

nodes.label: Open integration gates
nodes.rationale: Clean-from-zero disposable replay, real pairing, truly overlapping sessions, older RLS reruns and human screen-reader checks remain open.

nodes.label: Development Setup
nodes.rationale: Application checks and preview work without containers; real flows use verified managed Us-Together configuration.

nodes.label: Hosted database workflow
nodes.rationale: Verify saved project, review and apply migrations, run rollback-only negatives/advisors, regenerate types, then separately authorize empty-database replay.

nodes.label: Server-only project reference
nodes.rationale: SUPABASE_PROJECT_ID belongs only in ignored local environment; never substitute another connector-listed project or track credentials.

nodes.label: Optional local Supabase
nodes.rationale: Local runtime is an optional alternative; its test:rls command is not claimed passed by hosted evidence.

nodes.label: Testing Strategy
nodes.rationale: Layered unit, RLS, service, component, browser, build and security verification uses isolated fictional data.

nodes.label: Mandatory negative cases
nodes.rationale: Cross-tenant, private-note, secret-purchase, storage, reveal timing, former-member, ownership reassignment and projection non-inference tests.

nodes.label: Release checklist
nodes.rationale: Clean install/replay, all commands, advisors, negatives, desktop/mobile/a11y, secret safety and current documentation gate release.

nodes.label: Accessibility and design QA
nodes.rationale: Keyboard/manual screen reader, 200-percent reflow, non-color cues, reduced motion and rendered Impeccable review.

nodes.label: Master Prompt Traceability
nodes.rationale: Maps 81 source requirements to canonical specifications, delivery phases and verification evidence.

nodes.label: Traceability Coverage Gate
nodes.rationale: A requirement is covered only with canonical behavior and a named verification method; delivery or ownership changes require matrix updates.

nodes.label: Historical phase closure query
nodes.rationale: 2026-09-01 query recommended Phase 1-2 closure then later phases; retained as historical context, not current workflow authority.

nodes.label: Historical next-step query
nodes.rationale: 2026-09-01 query recommended waiting for local runtime and pairing gates before Phase 4. ADR-014 supersedes local prerequisite and pairing timing.

hyperedges.label: Hosted Phase 4 evidence with explicit limits
